title: Domain Event

validation.research: Evans's original accessible DDD Reference, Domain Events on printed page 13, establishes domain-significant occurrences, immutable fact data, and temporal/propagation concerns. Fowler's Domain Event source is explicitly identified as a draft and supports source data and occurrence versus observation time. Bogard supports recording independently of dispatch. Microsoft explains dispatch timing, participating transactions, and internal domain versus committed integration contracts. Richardson's original Outbox pattern supports durable publication intent and possible repeated delivery. Fowler's Event Sourcing draft supports the separate authoritative-history/reconstruction pattern. Official Python sources support frozen fields and aware UTC datetime behavior. The shipment policy, code, and native illustrations are original teaching material.
validation.python_examples: Both actual article blocks execute and produce all six stated lines exactly. Checks verify fact payload and identity/time snapshots, frozen fields, immutable datetime components, strict timezone.utc validation, rejection of malformed text, naive timestamps, other offsets, date-only inputs and datetime subclasses, invalid-input stability before mutation, readonly public status and pending properties, one accepted local dispatch, repeated-transition rejection without another fact, nondestructive tuple snapshots, pure independent description functions, retained original context across different shipments and times, opaque text preservation, and caller-supplied historical occurrence time. A separate shipment can reuse the supplied event ID, explicitly verifying that no allocator, global uniqueness enforcement, consumer inbox, or deduplication is silently implemented. The model imports only dataclasses and datetime and performs no I/O.

example_limits: Sequential in-memory Shipment ready-to-dispatched state with caller-provided opaque identity and strict UTC time. Accepted events are local pending facts until a surrounding transaction commits. Pure descriptions only return strings; no physical dispatch verification, database, transaction, rollback implementation, allocator, global uniqueness check, reliable dispatcher, broker, delivery, acknowledgement, replay, sequence protocol, consumer deduplication, or concurrent transition protection exists. Normal API immutability is not a security boundary. The separate outbox illustration describes a durable publishing design rather than implemented code; it distinguishes domain fact E1 from mapped message M1 and preserves message identity on resend. Handler dispatch timing, participating transaction boundaries, effect ordering, schema evolution, privacy, external idempotency, and pending-event cleanup require explicit production choices.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
